paraphrase: Dhṛtarāṣṭra asks Sañjaya: on the field of dharma (dharmakṣetra), the field of the Kurus (kurukṣetra), what did my people and the sons of Pāṇḍu do, assembled there and eager to fight?

notes: māmakāḥ ('my people') are Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons; pāṇḍavāḥ are the sons of Pāṇḍu. This is the only verse of the Gītā spoken by Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

paraphrase: Chapter 1 (47 verses) frames the dialogue and sets out the problem the teaching answers. 1.1: Dhṛtarāṣṭra asks Sañjaya what the two armies assembled at Kurukṣetra, 'the field of dharma', did. 1.2–11: Duryodhana approaches his teacher (Droṇa), names the leading warriors of the Pāṇḍava army and of his own, and urges that Bhīṣma be protected. 1.12–19: Bhīṣma's lion-roar and conch start a tumult; Kṛṣṇa, Arjuna and the Pāṇḍava leaders blow their named conches, and the sound tears the hearts of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons. 1.20–27: Arjuna asks Kṛṣṇa to station the chariot between the armies, and sees fathers, grandfathers, teachers, uncles, brothers, sons, friends and kinsmen on both sides. 1.28–46: overcome with compassion (kṛpā) and despondency (viṣāda), Arjuna describes his bodily collapse (1.29–30) and argues against fighting: no good comes from killing one's own people; he wants neither victory nor kingship; killing kin, even aggressors, brings sin; the destruction of a family destroys its dharmas, lets adharma prevail, corrupts the women, causes mixing of the classes (varṇasaṅkara), deprives the ancestors of their offerings and leads to hell; it would be better to be killed unresisting. 1.47: he sits down in the chariot, casting aside bow and arrows, his mind overwhelmed by sorrow (śoka).
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The colophon title (Arjunaviṣādayoga in the vulgate) is not part of the segments. Arjuna's arguments of 1.31–46 are answered by Kṛṣṇa from 2.2 onward (cf. 2.11, prajñāvādān).

paraphrase: Of the unreal (asat) there is no coming to be (bhāva); of the real (sat) there is no ceasing to be (abhāva). The conclusion (anta) about both of these has been seen by those who see the truth (tattvadarśin).

original.text:
vedāvināśinaṃ nityaṃ ya enamajamavyayam|
kathaṃ sa puruṣaḥ pārtha kaṃ ghātayati hanti kam

speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
vāsāṃsi jīrṇāni yathā vihāya

avyakto'yamacintyo'yamavikāryo'yamucyate|

avyaktādīni bhūtāni vyaktamadhyāni bhārata|

āścaryavatpaśyati kaścidena
māścaryavadvadati tathaiva cānyaḥ|
āścaryavaccainamanyaḥ śrṛṇoti

tasmātsarvāṇi bhūtāni na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi

original.text:
svadharmamapi cāvekṣya na vikampitumarhasi|
dharmyāddhi yuddhāchreyo'nyatkṣatriyasya na vidyate

original.text:
yadṛcchayā copapannaṃ svargadvāramapāvṛtam|

original.text:
eṣā te'bhihitā sāṃkhye buddhiryoge tvimāṃ śrṛṇu|
buddhyāyukto yayā pārtha karmabandhaṃ prahāsyasi

The segment's 'śrṛṇu' is a misspelling of śṛṇu; kept as in the segment.

vedavādaratāḥ pārtha nānyadastīti vādinaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

speaker: Kṛṣṇa

original.text:
traiguṇyaviṣayā vedā nistraiguṇyo bhavārjuna|
nirdvandvo nityasattvastho niryogakṣema ātmavān
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: nityasattvastha is taken as 'ever abiding in (the guṇa) sattva' or as 'ever abiding in the real (sattva = being)'; the commentators divide. yogakṣema: acquiring what one lacks and keeping what one has. ātmavān: 'self-possessed, heedful'.

original.text:

notes: Read either as: for the knower all the Vedas are of no more use than a well in a flood (their purposes are contained in his knowledge), or as: the knower takes from the Vedas only what serves his purpose, as one takes from a reservoir; the commentators divide.

mā karmaphalaheturbhūrmā te saṅgo'stvakarmaṇi

paraphrase: This is the state of brahman (brāhmī sthiti), Pārtha; having attained it one is no longer deluded. Abiding in it even at the time of death (antakāla), one attains the nirvāṇa of brahman (brahmanirvāṇa).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: antakāle 'pi: 'even at the time of death' (the commentators add: all the more if it is reached earlier in life). The compound brahmanirvāṇa recurs at 5.24–26. The segment has no colophon.

paraphrase: Chapter 2 (72 verses) begins the teaching. 2.1–10: Kṛṣṇa rebukes Arjuna's faintness of heart (2.2–3); Arjuna restates his dilemma about fighting his revered elders, declares himself Kṛṣṇa's disciple who has taken refuge and asks what is better (2.4–8), then says he will not fight (2.9); Kṛṣṇa, as if smiling, replies (2.10). 2.11–30: the argument from the embodied one (dehin): the wise do not grieve; neither Kṛṣṇa, Arjuna nor the kings ever were not or will not be; the embodied one passes through bodies as through the ages of life and as one changes clothes; the unreal has no being and the real no non-being; the embodied one is indestructible, unborn, eternal, neither slays nor is slain, cannot be cut, burnt, wetted or dried, is unmanifest and unthinkable — so grief is misplaced; even if it were born and died again and again, death is certain for the born, and grief would still be unfit (2.26–28). 2.31–38: the argument from Arjuna's own dharma (svadharma) and honour: a battle in accordance with dharma is the best thing for a kṣatriya and an open door to heaven; refusing brings sin and disgrace; fight with pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat made the same. 2.39–53: the same understanding (buddhi) 'according to yoga': no effort is lost; resolute understanding is one; those who delight in Vedic words aimed at heaven and power lack it; the Vedas deal with the three guṇas — be beyond them; the entitlement is to action, not its fruits; yoga is equanimity (samatva) and skill in actions; the wise, abandoning the fruit, are freed from the bondage of birth; understanding immovable in samādhi attains yoga. 2.54–72: Arjuna asks about the one of steady wisdom (sthitaprajña); Kṛṣṇa describes him: free of desires, content in the self, unshaken by pain and pleasure, withdrawing the senses like a tortoise; the fall from dwelling on objects through attachment, desire, anger and delusion to ruin (2.62–63), and the rise through senses free of passion and aversion to serenity (prasāda), steady understanding and peace (2.64–66); the sage awake in the night of beings; peace like the ocean receiving the rivers; the brāhmī sthiti, which, held even at death, attains brahmanirvāṇa.
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The chapter itself (2.39) labels what precedes as understanding 'according to sāṃkhya' and what follows as 'according to yoga'. The colophon title (Sāṃkhyayoga in the vulgate) is not part of the segments.

original.text:
niyataṃ kuru karma tvaṃ karma jyāyo hyakarmaṇaḥ|

original.text:
yajñārthātkarmaṇo'nyatra loko'yaṃ karmabandhanaḥ|
tadarthaṃ karma kaunteya muktasaṃgaḥ samācara

original.text:
sahayajñāḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā purovāca prajāpatiḥ|
anena prasaviṣyadhvameṣa vo'stviṣṭakāmadhuk

original.text:

parasparaṃ bhāvayantaḥ śreyaḥ paramavāpsyatha

translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
iṣṭānbhogānhi vo devā dāsyante yajñabhāvitāḥ|
tairdattānapradāyaibhyo yo bhuṅkte stena eva saḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

original.text:
yajñaśiṣṭāśinaḥ santo mucyante sarvakilbiṣaiḥ|
bhuñjate te tvaghaṃ pāpā ye pacantyātmakāraṇāt

original.text:
annādbhavanti bhūtāni parjanyādannasambhavaḥ|

original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

speaker: Kṛṣṇa

original.text:
karma brahmodbhavaṃ viddhi brahmākṣarasamudbhavam|
tasmātsarvagataṃ brahma nityaṃ yajñe pratiṣṭhitam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Know that action arises from brahman, and brahman arises from the imperishable (akṣara); therefore the all-pervading (sarvagata) brahman is ever established in sacrifice.

original.text:

aghāyurindriyārāmo moghaṃ pārtha sa jīvati

original.text:
yastvātmaratireva syādātmatṛptaśca mānavaḥ|
ātmanyeva ca santuṣṭastasya kāryaṃ na vidyate

original.text:

original.text:

original.text:

original.text:
mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi saṃnyasyādhyātmacetasā|

original.text:

original.text:
ye tvetadabhyasūyanto nānutiṣṭhanti me matam|
sarvajñānavimūḍhāṃstānviddhi naṣṭānacetasaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

original.text:
sadṛśaṃ ceṣṭate svasyāḥ prakṛterjñānavānapi|
prakṛtiṃ yānti bhūtāni nigrahaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati

translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
śreyānsvadharmo viguṇaḥ paradharmātsvanuṣṭhitāt|

original.text:

paraphrase: Chapter 3 (43 verses) answers Arjuna's question why, if understanding is superior, he is urged to act. 3.1–2: Arjuna asks for the one thing that leads to the good. 3.3–9: Kṛṣṇa names two commitments (niṣṭhā) — jñānayoga for the Sāṃkhyas, karmayoga for the Yogins; freedom from action does not come by not acting nor perfection by mere renunciation; no one can remain without acting, since the guṇas of prakṛti make all act; restraining the organs of action while dwelling on objects in the mind is hypocrisy; one who acts with the organs of action, the senses controlled, unattached, excels; do prescribed action; action other than for sacrifice binds, so act for sacrifice without attachment. 3.10–16: the wheel of sacrifice: Prajāpati created beings with sacrifice; gods and humans nourish one another; one who enjoys without offering is a thief; eating the remainder of sacrifice frees from faults; beings–food–rain–sacrifice–action–brahman–the imperishable; one who does not turn the wheel lives in vain. 3.17–19: for one content in the self nothing remains to be done; therefore act unattached and attain the highest. 3.20–26: holding the world together (lokasaṃgraha): Janaka and others reached perfection by action; the best person sets the standard; Kṛṣṇa, who has nothing to attain, still acts lest the worlds perish; the knower should act unattached as the ignorant act attached, without unsettling their understanding. 3.27–29: the guṇas act; the one deluded by ahaṃkāra thinks 'I am the doer'; the knower of the truth is unattached. 3.30–32: renounce all actions in Kṛṣṇa and fight; those who follow this teaching with faith are freed, those who carp are lost. 3.33–35: beings follow their nature; passion and aversion in the senses are waylayers; one's own dharma, even imperfect, is better than another's. 3.36–43: asked what drives a person to sin against his will, Kṛṣṇa names desire and anger, born of rajas, the enemy that covers knowledge and is seated in the senses, mind and understanding; control the senses first, know what is beyond the understanding, and slay desire.

notes: The colophon title (Karmayoga in the vulgate) is not part of the segments. Chapter 4 continues with the lineage of this yoga (4.1–3: Vivasvat, Manu, Ikṣvāku).
